design_revision: Written after a visual check of the first frames and before any recorded run; no bound changed. The bounds file describes a level camera at the origin with the ground at y = -1.6. The first frame from it was half sky, with the spheres in a band at the horizon, and the front row hid the rows behind it. The committed field puts the camera above and in front (eye (0, 2.4, 3) looking at (0, -0.5, -6.5)), with the ground at y = -1.0 and spheres of radius 0.6 in rows at 3.5 to 10.7 m. Everything is expressed in view space (spheres, ground quad, light, and the sky cube built from the procedural sky turned into view space), because lighting.hpp works in view space. Tangents follow path tracer v3's rule in view space.

f4_pt_error.prediction_check: I predicted a miss of 0.6 to 0.9 carried by the ground. That was wrong: under this sky the sun's cast shadows are soft and small next to the sky's light, so the ground's error is 0.2. Most of the error sits in the glass looks, where the raster's one-interface model meets a refracting sphere.

f5_frame_times.observed: Wall times, not frame times: they include building the samples, the tables, pipeline creation, uploads and readback, and the shading dispatch is not timed on its own. CPU float64 frame (GCC, all threads) 1.49 s at 256 x 160 x 4; MSVC 1.24 s, and 2.32 s at 1920 x 1080. GPU shading command, RTX 4090: 3.98 s at 256 x 160, 10.66 s at 1080p; WARP 7.94 s at 256 x 160. Path-traced reference (GCC, 4 threads, 512 samples at each of 4 points a pixel, 8 bounces): 199 s. A dispatch-only GPU timer is an open item.

does_not_prove: Real-time frame rates for a full renderer (there is no dispatch timer yet); anything on a laptop GPU (none available); that the raster is right for glass.
